quick: Commonly 90 to 180 mg per dose in combination tablets, two to three times daily
summary: Bromelain is a mixture of cysteine proteases from pineapple stem. In India it is sold mainly in fixed combinations with trypsin and rutoside as an adjunct for post-traumatic and post-operative swelling. Clinical evidence is modest and it is not an approved medicine in the US, Canada or EU.
indications: Adjunct for post-operative or post-traumatic oedema and inflammation (usually with trypsin and rutoside)

dosage.d: Commonly 90 to 180 mg per dose in combination tablets, two to three times daily
dosage.n: Take on an empty stomach for systemic enzyme effect; follow the combination product's pack

admin: Swallow enteric-coated tablets whole; do not crush
moa: Proteolytic activity is thought to reduce bradykinin and fibrin deposition at sites of inflammation, decreasing oedema. Part of an oral dose is absorbed intact; the size of the clinical effect is uncertain.

absolute: Allergy to pineapple, bromelain or papain
relative: Bleeding disorders or concurrent anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy

preg: Safety not established; use only if clearly needed
lact: Safety not established; weigh benefit against unknown risk

major: Warfarin and other anticoagulants: additive bleeding risk
moderate: Antiplatelet drugs and NSAIDs: bleeding risk
May increase absorption of amoxicillin and tetracyclines

serious: Hypersensitivity, including cross-reactivity with latex, wheat and pollen

monitoring: Bleeding or bruising in patients on anticoagulants
counsel: Use exactly as the pack directs
Stop and seek care for rash, swelling or breathing difficulty
missed: Take it when remembered unless the next dose is due; do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote. Supportive and symptomatic care.
